newsitem.title: INDIA: HPCL says India owes it about 10 bln.
newsitem.headline: HPCL says India owes it about 10 bln.

text.p: India's Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd said on Wednesday that the government owes it about 10 billion rupees in dues from the oil pool account.
"The oil pool deficit has affected our financial resources somewhat," HPCL chairman H.L. Zutshi told a news conference on Wednesday.
"But we are tiding over the problem through judicious use of funds," he said. "None of our projects are affected because of this," Zutshi added.
Answering a question, HPCL's finance director S.D. Gupta said "interest burden this year (1996/97 April-March) would go up by 320 to 350 million rupees".
HPCL has already provided for an interest cost of 375.2 million rupees for the six months ended September 30, 1996.
HPCL said it would convert warrants into equity shares beginning on February 24 at a price of 340 rupees per share of 10 rupees face value against the current market price of 385 rupees.
